study.question: Conditional on the existing target-relation rank bank, does allowing relation-specific compression of zeroth-order content S improve four-task prediction beyond balanced rotated sharing and redundant rank-map capacity?
study.hypothesis: Different target-match relations retain different useful embedding coordinates. The current shared slot_projection maps each 112-dimensional S through the same 32-dimensional content projection; only M already has a relation-specific map. A separate, time-consistent D[r]*S before the fixed interaction can preserve relation-dependent content information better than shared projection alone. This is a function-class change on existing summaries, not additional sample information or a proven information bottleneck.

nearest_work.difference: Pinned benchmark source lines148-201 uses field-wise tokenization and per-token FFNs. Adapt heterogeneous transformations to overlapping target-match summary groups, with one linear residual bank shared across five temporal bins. No HiFormer blocks or task tokens copied. Original paper paper:hiformer has link-only access; original-method equivalence and novelty are unverified.

Archived primary text lines272-283 supports unnormalized target activation and describes sequence limitations. Preserve inherited unnormalized activation; test relation-dependent summary projection rather than claiming a new attention or sequence method.

Pinned forward lines175-195 flattens raw field/history embeddings before chunk tokenization. Current study keeps masked S/M pooling and adds no raw-event access; full flattening is a considered future replacement, not tested here.

inherited_components: Entire g0-r0008-relation_bank architecture and CONFIG, excluding the new content_bank_mode choice.
Six released item-field embeddings plus action; target action zeroed; invalid history IDs sanitized before Dice/embedding.
DIN local activation, raw static/global-pool bypass, temporal quartiles, seven overlapping target relations, shared slot_projection including explicit count.
Full linear rank moment, duplicate full moment projection and stable relation-specific rank bank, all unchanged.
Masked JointBlock, token identities and all four task towers, default sum of unweighted BCEs.
study.proposed_difference: Write token z[t,r]=P([S[t,r],count[t,r]])+A*M[t,r]+B*M[t,r]+C[r]*M[t,r]+D[route(t,r)]*X[t,r]. D has 7x112x32 bias-free zero-initialized parameters appended after all inherited initialization. Candidate X=S and route=r; rotated control X=S and route=(r+t)%7; duplicate-rank control X=M and route=r; replay X=S and added output multiplied by zero. All arms retain inherited C[r]. Counts, masks, summary dimension and token identity are unchanged. Every file is standalone.
predictions: Primary predeclared ordering to support the complete hypothesis: relation_content beats rotated_content, duplicate_rank and zero_content on validation equal-weight four-task macro AUC. No undeclared task veto; also report all task AUC/Logloss changes and costs.

The aligned-versus-rotated contrast isolates sharing conditional on the extra S channel; aligned-versus-duplicate-rank tests whether an independent content channel adds value beyond redundant optimization. These contrasts do not prove an information-theoretic bottleneck.

At initialization every new arm equals the current parent prediction function for fixed inherited state; changes to padded IDs or current action remain irrelevant. New content residual is exactly zero for no-match groups and empty histories.

Secondary exploratory diagnostics use the existing 0,1-16,17-64,>64 history bins; no assumed monotonic slice benefit. Zero history residual is zero, but trained static predictions may still differ because training is joint.
falsifiers: A relation_content tie/loss against rotated_content defeats the time-consistent relation-sharing explanation for this implementation.
A relation_content tie/loss against duplicate_rank or zero_content does not support independent content compression as the cause of a gain.
If a gain disappears in paired validation repetitions or is comparable to replay drift, retain it as an unresolved single-seed observation rather than a confirmed mechanism.

Nonfinite outputs/gradients, inherited-state mismatch, changed prediction identities, padding sensitivity, current-label dependence or host budget overflow invalidate the run; do not change the frozen protocol to repair it.
alternative_explanations: Optimization or dense-gradient clipping changes from extra active parameters, rather than better semantic representation.
Extra functional capacity or different scale of S versus M; same parameter count is not equal effective capacity.
Unequal occupancy, relation overlap and target-category/brand auxiliary label semantics can make semantic grouping useful only on this offline benchmark.
Single-seed chance and repeated adaptive validation selection across many trajectories; no formal significance claim is justified.
Inherited whole-window vocabulary and delayed-feedback visibility assumptions; production point-in-time validity remains unestablished.
